A13 census rules, logged before the script is written or run (G45's order test): (1) each ruled line takes the class it was ruled under (instantiate, restrict, add-condition and add-step spec files), checked against its written decision and kind, and a re-ruled line takes its re-ruling's class: the order by the hours (O-IN, O-OUT, O-TR, S-O-*), the order named in words (M-IN, M-TR, S-M-*), the bound (BOUND, S-BOUND), the second path (SP, S-SP), one act or not orderable (J, EL-J), not help after upkeep (NH, EL-NH), one end (ONE, EL-ONE), held by another statement (S-HELD), after the close (AFTER), particulars apart (P-G6; detroitredwings-036, tagged PO, shows the order and is counted with the order rooms but marked); absent rejects are the order with an ungraded direction, absent particulars are other, absent accepts with kind none are limits. (2) Direction of the first help after the upkeep, from the class: the room asks or receives (IN, the mechanism's direction), gives or offers (OUT, help from spare capacity in G17's add-line reading), or trades (TR). (3) Tags: R on order lines (the upkeep named from the room's record), JM on J lines (the night shortage named). (4) A room is counted in each class its lines show, then once by priority: order, bound, second path, one act, held, not help, one end, after the close, other, limit. (5) Shares: the order among rooms with an episode (the order, the bound or the second path), as G36 and G38 counted episodes, then with one-act rooms added to the denominator; the order in words among order rooms; the direction of the first help among order lines and order rooms; beside C2's 171 of 240 (0.713, null p95 0.642), its 106 transitions in 44 rooms and the counterexample response's 69 of 240. Lines exist where labelers saw both elements, so these are counts of ruled lines, not rates in the population
